STRATEGY: The parent is a conditional/forgiving strategy (slot 5) that cooperates for the first 4 rounds, then retaliates to consecutive defections and uses rate checks. The trace simulates probing/defecting against each peer slot (0–11) to map retaliation thresholds and endgame behavior. It proposes an adaptive strategy that probes with early defections, exploits forgiving opponents, and defects in the last rounds.

STRATEGY: The parent is a generous tit-for-tat variant that cooperates, retaliates to recent defections, and defects late based on opponent defections. The trace simulates the 12 peer strategies and their thresholds, especially slot 0, 4, 5, and 7. It proposes changing to an adaptive classifier that probes early, detects forgiving vs retaliatory opponents, and adjusts endgame defection.

--- PART 4/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe the best approach is to use a strategy that is similar to the top performer (slot 11) but with some improvements. Slot 11 scored 282."
STRATEGY: The parent is a forgiving tit-for-tat core that probes at round 2, then adapts: in RETALIATORY mode it cooperates until round 99 and defects only at 99; in FORGIVING mode it defects on even rounds while the opponent keeps cooperating, switching to RETALIATORY if the opponent defects. The trace simulates this against slots 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and pure TFT, computing endgame payoffs for k defections. It changes the parent by adding an early probe, a forgiveness/retaliation mode switch, and an alternating-defection exploitation rule.

--- PART 5/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's compare to parent (slot 4). Parent score is 276. Our strategy might score around 300+ against forgiving ones, and lose a few against retaliatory."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like policy that cooperates until late, then defects if opponent defections reach a threshold. The trace simulates a revised policy: probe with D at round 2, C at round 3, then FORGIVING mode (alternate D on even rounds, C on odd) unless the opponent ever defects, in which case switch to RET mode (cooperate until round 99, then defect). It changes the parent by adding the round-2 probe, the FORGIVING alternating exploitation, and the switch to RET mode on any observed opponent defection.

--- PART 6/6 ---

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the rule: if opponent has any D in history, switch to RET (always C until 99, then D). Else, FORGIVING (alternate D/C on even/odd). This is simple and robust."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates until late, then defects if opponent has defected at least 3 times; simulated against 12 peer slots and archive; changed to probe with D at round 2, switch to always-C if any opponent D appears, otherwise alternate D on even rounds and C on odd, with D at round 99.
